title: Grace in Salvation
definition: Grace in Salvation is God’s undeserved favor by which He saves sinners through Jesus Christ apart from their merit or works.
summary: Grace in Salvation is God’s undeserved favor by which He saves sinners through Jesus Christ apart from their merit or works.
christFocus: Jesus displays the grace of God by receiving the undeserving, dying for sinners, and giving salvation as a gift rather than a wage earned.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Grace means salvation begins in God’s mercy, not human worthiness. Scripture does not present grace as God helping basically good people finish the job; grace is God rescuing the guilty, helpless, and undeserving through Christ.

Grace does not excuse sin or leave people unchanged. The same grace that forgives also trains believers to deny ungodliness and walk in newness of life. Grace saves, teaches, strengthens, and keeps.

Christ is the fullness of saving grace. In Him, God does not merely offer sinners a second chance; He gives forgiveness, righteousness, adoption, the Spirit, and a new future that rests on His kindness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people believe God only welcomes them when they are strong, clean, useful, or impressive. Grace speaks directly to the rejected, addicted, disabled, ashamed, and weary: salvation is a gift from Christ, not a reward for being enough.

Grace also protects believers from pride. No one stands before God by superiority, background, knowledge, or effort. Every saved person stands by mercy.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive salvation as grace, not achievement. Let God’s kindness lead you to repentance, worship, humility, and Spirit-empowered obedience rather than shame-driven striving or self-righteous pride.
